page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top with the page number to its left. Text in one block: the first two lines run full width above the figure. Below them a narrow column of text wraps around a diagram (two circles meeting at f, with points a, b, c) on the right. Further down, a second group of small diagrams (A, B, and a triangle) sits to the right of the text. Full-width text continues below. A catchword sits at the lower right.

main_text.p: duas partes æquales, ducantur ergo duo circuli; vnus positopede circini in c, alter posito pede circini in b vbi hi duo circuli inuicem cocurrunt nimirum in f, ibi ducatur linea in a. Dico ꝗ linea fa secet angulum fa in duos angulos æquales. Demonstratio sumitur ex ratione circuli, quia anguli æquantur suis cruribus. At vero crura hic sunt æqualia, quia sunt radii æqualium circulorum, nam c.a est radius circuli g.b: a.est radius circuli h. æqual͂ autem circulorum radii sunt inter se æquales. Hinc etiam non difficile est Angulum angulo æqualem efficere, in angulo dato (exempli gratia) A ex intimo angulo describe arcus α.β. in anguli cruribus: deinde pares angulos in data linea B (ex qua angulum angulo A æqualem deducere debes) describe γ.δ.ȝ. ex α. duc arcum per β. & huic parem ex γ. per δ. per intersectionem tandem in δ. duc rectam ex B & erit angulus angulo A æqualis, siue fiat in angulis acutis siue obtusis.
Et tantum de Linea & Lineato siue Angulo: sequitur doctrina Geometrica de Figuris.

page.notes: The circle diagram carries the letters a, b, c, f, g, h and the arc marks; the two small figures carry A, B, α, β, γ, δ, ȝ. Both are reproduced only as described above. The text is set around the figures, so the line order follows the printed reading order. Some letters in the diagrams and the old forms (long s written as s) are approximate.
